track: injection (source mined+injected; 12 traps: T1-T7,T11,T12 real upstream code, T8-T10 injected)

b1.summary: Two opposite failure modes around one area. DeepSeek over-hardens: all 31 security tests pass in runs 1-2 but owner/admin bypass of a deny-all bucket, the open-by-default embedding authenticator and the trusted local shell break (reward forced to 0). MiMo under-fixes: all 226 functional tests pass in runs 1-2 but the Iceberg catalog's name-only caller path (T3) and name-only 'admin' (T6) stay open, plus catalog denials returned as 500 (T12). DS run 3 and MM run 3 mix both. A 7th MiMo record (start 2026-10-20T09:33, same minute as graded MiMo run 1) has an empty reward, no failing list and no audit; it was treated as a duplicate/aborted trial record and excluded, so MiMo counts 3 graded runs. Functional-failure fairness: TestFuncZZShell* are fair keep-working regressions (instruction Preservation bullet 5: 'trusted local administration tooling ... that act for an account they name'); TestFuncZZCatalogEmbeddedAuthenticatorOpenDefault is fair (Preservation bullet 4 'requests that carry no credentials on a deployment with no identities configured' + 'The properties hold for every deployment, however that deployment authenticates its callers'; the test's authenticator has no identities and DefaultAllow=true, zz_s3t_func_test.go:257-268); TestFuncZZAdminsBypassBucketPolicy is fair by the letter ('keep working exactly as today: an owner acting on its own resources; identities granted administrative ... permissions') but is a value trap against AWS-style deny-overrides intuition, and the instruction itself says 'an explicit deny always applies' for credential-less requests (FAIRNESS.md rates it medium).

b4.note: Every run fails in the Iceberg catalog / embedding-authenticator / trusted-tooling area (T3/T6 security or their coupled preservation tests); TestFuncZZCatalogEmbeddedAuthenticatorOpenDefault fails in 4 of 6 runs. DeepSeek errs toward over-blocking, MiMo toward leaving the name-only catalog caller open. No run failed any test at the three injected sites (T8 usage, T9 batch delete, T10 catalog index) or at T1/T2/T4/T5/T7/T11.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md (2026-10-20 11:50, reviews the upgraded 31-security-test version that was trialled) ends 'NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES': confirm (1) catalog namespace listings of a foreign bucket must be refused, not served empty (TestSecZZCatalogOtherUserCannotListNamespaces 'any 2xx fails, even an empty list'; also the GET in TestSecZZCatalogRefusalsAreClientErrors), and (2) a refused batch delete must be all-or-nothing. Unresolved in the files. Outcome-neutral: (2) decided no run; (1) appears only in MiMo runs 2-3, each of which has other independent failures (T3 security misses, or functional regressions).

b6.reason: Upstream fix b13463880 (fetched) adds manager.SetDefaultAllow(authenticator.DefaultAllow()) in iceberg/server.go, a defaultAllowFor() that treats a name-only identity as authenticated, SetTrusted(true) for the shell, and the admin-account check in getAccountID. So the most frequent decisive cluster (T3 name-only catalog caller: NameOnlyCaller*, OtherUserCannotListNamespaces) and the coupled preservation (embedded open-default, trusted shell) are modelled by the public fix. Not covered: T6 name-only 'admin' (getAccountID still falls back to the identity name 'admin'; notes: still open on master) which decided DS3 and MM1, T12 catalog denial->500 mapping (decided MM2, MM3), and the owner/admin deny-bypass preservation (DS1, DS2; upstream leaves it as is). Every run keeps at least one failure the upstream fix does not address, but a look-up model would lose the T3 misses and likely the over-hardening, leaving MM2/MM3-type runs decided only by the contract-form T12 test.

quotes: for every element of a request that names more than one resource
neither may be chosen by an identifier the request supplies
Only an identity granted administrative permissions is an administrator
a request without valid credentials never acts as an owner or an administrator, whatever else it carries

The open-by-default fallback — access granted when no access rule decides — applies only to requests that carry no credentials: a deployment with no identities configured, and requests served as a configured anonymous identity.
The properties hold for every deployment, however that deployment authenticates its callers.
Fix the flaw and its close variants

b8.gate: .sound (qa_tasks.json; no gate_verdict.json in the build folder; notes: nop 31/31 security fail + functional pass, oracle passes x3, 20/20 patch checks)
b8.blind: not run (no blind_status.txt; static gate notes 'missing blind pass patch' left for others)
b8.note: Two alternative designs score 1.0 per notes: hardening.patch (oracle + defensive checks) and alt_principal_default.patch (centralised principal/open-default design at a different layer). Reference fix touches 21 files, so the task is large but solvable.

c1.mechanism: authz / tenant isolation: principal mis-derivation (shared admin account, IdP claims, name-only 'admin', client header) plus open-by-default fallback applied to authenticated callers, across two front ends (S3 Tables API and Iceberg REST catalog)
c1.domain: distributed object store (SeaweedFS S3 gateway, S3 Tables, Iceberg catalog)

c2.origin: published-far-site + uncovered-upstream + keep-working-value (injected sites never decisive)
c2.pattern: missed indirect route (second front end, name-only caller) / over-blocked legitimate use
c2.note: Decisive traps: T3 (published-fix site on the catalog front end), T6 and T12 (real upstream code the fix does not touch), and coupled preservation values (owner/admin bypass of deny-all, open-default embedding, trusted shell). The breaker is carried by the mined real-code levers, not by the injection.

d2.evidence: Plausible: handler_bucket_usage.go and handler_table_batch.go copy the house style exactly (getExtendedAttribute/readTags, CheckPermissionWithContext with PolicyContext, writeError codes), are dispatched from the real HandleRequest switch, and add request/response types in types.go; handlers_index.go is registered beside the real catalog routes with s.Auth. Planted signs: the batch handler's doc comment rationalises the flaw ('the remaining tables are removed with that same authorization decision so a large delete does not re-read the bucket policy for every table'); the usage handler adds a one-use accountIDFromARN helper to take the owner from the caller's ARN while metadata.OwnerAccountID is read in the same function and returned in the response; the index walks the filer directly instead of the existing ListTables path (FAIRNESS.md: 'the one sibling I would call designed-to-flaw'); all three are new operations with no other callers, tests or docs (GetTableBucketUsage/BatchDeleteTables are not upstream ops). Effect: both models fixed all three injected sites in all 6 runs (TestSecZZUsageIgnoresCallerSuppliedOwner, ...BatchDeleteChecksEveryTable, ...CatalogIndexHidesOtherTables never failed).

e1.why: DeepSeek 0/3 and MiMo 0/3 graded (one ungraded duplicate MiMo record excluded).

e2.why: 6/6 failing runs audited trustworthy, model-failed, high confidence.

e3.why: READY (gate_a) and current, but FAIRNESS.md leaves NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES open (listing refuse-vs-empty; batch all-or-nothing); outcome-neutral for the 6 runs.

e4.why: DS3, MM1, MM2 are decided by security misses (T3 name-only catalog caller, T6 name-only admin).

e5.why: T6 (DS3, MM1) and T12 (MM2, MM3) are not touched by upstream fix b13463880; but the most frequent security miss, T3, is covered upstream.

concerns: Injected siblings contributed nothing: no run failed T8/T9/T10, so this is effectively a mined real-code breaker; it says little in favour of the injection pipeline.

Half the runs (DS1, DS2, and MM3 apart from a contract test) are decided purely by keep-working regressions; TestFuncZZAdminsBypassBucketPolicy is fair by 'exactly as today' but cuts against deny-overrides intuition and the instruction's own 'an explicit deny always applies' sentence (FAIRNESS medium).

TestFuncZZCatalogEmbeddedAuthenticatorOpenDefault decides 4/6 runs; its fairness rests on reading an embedding authenticator with an empty name map + DefaultAllow as 'a deployment with no identities configured'.
Open-internet: the public fix models the T3 cluster and the open-default/shell preservation; remaining uncovered decisive traps are T6 and the contract-form T12 (500 vs 4xx).
Open human-review question in FAIRNESS.md (listing refuse-vs-empty, batch all-or-nothing) never closed, though outcome-neutral.
Instruction paraphrases most trap shapes as explicit rules (multi-resource element, request-supplied identifiers, name-only/IdP admin, every authentication method); models failed anyway.
Blind fix never run; a 7th MiMo record is ungraded with no explanation in the data.
one_line: SeaweedFS table-storage tenant isolation where DeepSeek over-hardens (breaks owner/admin deny bypass, open-default embedding, trusted shell) and MiMo leaves the Iceberg catalog's name-only caller and name-only 'admin' open, while the three injected siblings were fixed in every run.
